candidates.evidence: Top matcher hit (CRD row 2666, R-3m) and the only library-matched candidate in the 60 to 1100 cm-1 window. The 181.4 cm-1 line sits about 6 cm-1 above the A1g2 position of few-quintuple-layer Bi2Se3 at 488 nm (about 174 to 176 cm-1, read by eye from Fig. 4 of arXiv:1201.5678). The strong E2g (about 131 cm-1) and A1g1 (about 72 cm-1) modes that Fig. 4 shows as the dominant lines are absent. The weak 140.2 cm-1 shoulder is about 9 cm-1 from E2g. The intensity pattern argues against Bi2Se3; it is kept as the best of the weak options, not as an identification.

Matcher (CRD row 3497) matches only the 181.4 cm-1 line as A1g with frequency scale 1.041. The 140.2 cm-1 shoulder is unmatched. The known strong 2H-MoTe2 modes near 170 to 173 and 290 cm-1 are not what the matcher reports. Weak evidence; not supported by the spectrum beyond one line.

Matcher (CRD row 1012) matches 181.4 cm-1 as Ag and 140.2 cm-1 as B3g. The reference Ag mode at 172.9 cm-1 is reported missing but is weak (relative intensity 0.13). Weak evidence from two line positions only.

hint_reasoning: No material hint was given (material_hint null, task identify). The working-directory name was not used as evidence. The spectrum does not establish a material. The matcher's top hit (Bi2Se3) is inconsistent with the expected intensity pattern.

peaks.assignment: unassigned in the strict sense; tentatively A1g (Bi2Se3 A1g2 if Bi2Se3)
peaks.source: Position and FWHM from rl_fit.py (single Lorentzian, 181.36 +/- 0.06 cm-1, FWHM 8.6 to 8.8 cm-1) and a 120 to 240 cm-1 two-component fit (181.36 +/- 0.06, FWHM 8.82 +/- 0.20). Label is inferred from the CRD Bi2Se3 A1g entry (Bagheri and Komsa 2023, Sci. Data 10, 80, row 2666, scale 1.01). Position compared with Fig. 4 of arXiv:1201.5678 (A1g2 about 174 to 176 cm-1 at 488 nm, by eye). Not a confirmed assignment.

peaks.assignment: unassigned weak shoulder; matcher suggests Eg (CRD row 2666) but that is inconsistent with Bi2Se3 Eg2 near 131
peaks.source: Two-component fit in 120 to 240 cm-1: centre 140.2 +/- 0.9 cm-1, FWHM 10.6 +/- 3.9 cm-1, amplitude 911 +/- 165 counts (about 7 percent of the main line; about 5.5 sigma). Residual rms falls from 344 to 303 counts when it is added. Not reported by the default fitter threshold (rl_fit.py without --min-snr).

citations: Fig. 4 of arXiv:1201.5678 (Bi2Se3 few-quintuple-layer Raman, 10 to 250 cm-1, 488 nm; E2g, A1g1 and A1g2 positions read by eye)
Bagheri and Komsa 2023, Sci. Data 10, 80 (Computational Raman Database, row 2666 Bi2Se3 R-3m; row 3497 MoTe2; row 1012 GeSe)
Mondal et al. 2025, npj 2D Mater., arXiv 2410.22164 (CrSBr Ag modes at 114, 244, 344 cm-1; used to rule out CrSBr)
Pawbake et al. 2023, Phys. Rev. B 107, 075421, arXiv 2211.12939 (CrSBr bulk Ag modes, same ruling out)
limits: The spectrum has one strong line (181.4 cm-1, SNR about 36) and one weak shoulder (140 cm-1). With so few lines, several DFT candidates match equally, so the material is not identified. The best guess is Bi2Se3 at low confidence (0.2).

Bi2Se3 is disfavoured. The E2g (about 131 cm-1) and A1g1 (about 72 cm-1) modes, which are the strongest lines in the Fig. 4 reference, are absent. The 532 nm excitation here differs from the 488 nm reference, but that is unlikely to remove both modes. The A1g2 position is about 6 cm-1 high of the reference value; the reference value was read by eye from a figure, not from a table. Sample thickness is unknown, so a thickness-dependent shift cannot be ruled in or out.

The matcher's missing-strong-mode penalty did not flag Bi2Se3's 72 and 131 cm-1 modes, and did not flag MoTe2's strong modes near 290 cm-1 either. This suggests the penalty is unreliable for single-line input. The ranking is therefore not treated as evidence.

CrSBr is ruled out: its Ag modes are at 114, 244 and 344 cm-1, and none is present here. Other curated materials (MoS2, WS2, MoSe2, WSe2, graphene, hBN, black phosphorus) were not directly tested by a lookup; the matcher returned no strong match for them.

A broad elevated background of about 700 to 800 counts between about 140 and 250 cm-1 sits above the decreasing trend (about 6000 counts at 60 cm-1, about 5100 at 1000 cm-1). It could be fluorescence or a broad band. It was not assigned or fitted as a peak, and the 532 nm excitation could induce photoluminescence.
Weak residual bumps at 392, 796, 848 and 888 cm-1 reach about 3 sigma in a smoothed residual. They are below the fitter threshold and are not reported as peaks.
No Si line near 520.7 cm-1 is present, so no substrate line is reported. The substrate is unknown.

No polarization data, no angle series, no layer-number relation, no reference spectrum on the same substrate and no instrument resolution were given. Layer number, strain, doping and defect density cannot be estimated. FWHM of about 8.8 cm-1 cannot be interpreted without a resolution reference.
QC found no cosmic-ray spikes and no saturation.
A tool output noted a held-out evaluation entry (Wdowik et al. 2025); I did not consult or use it.
